items.title: v2.1.172
items.bullet_md: - 🛠 **[v2.1.172](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.172)** — _Claude Code releases_. — Sub-agents can now recursively spawn their own sub-agents up to 5 levels deep. Amazon Bedrock region resolution follows AWS SDK precedence from ~/.aws config, and sessions using 1M context without credits no longer get permanently stuck.

score_components.taste_reason: Recursive sub-agents (5 levels deep) meaningfully extends the agent-pattern space; concrete changelog from the official Claude Code releases feed, extends state-of-ai's v2.1.157 row.

items.title: Give GitHub Copilot CLI real code intelligence with language servers
items.bullet_md: - 🛠 **[Give GitHub Copilot CLI real code intelligence with language servers](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/give-github-copilot-cli-real-code-intelligence-with-language-servers/)** — _GitHub AI blog_. — LSP integration gives Copilot CLI real-time type checking and symbol resolution instead of brute-force text search. The setup works with any language server through a simple configuration file.

score_components.taste_reason: LSP-driven code intelligence replaces brute-force text search in Copilot CLI — practical quality-of-life improvement with a concrete config-based setup, GitHub blog is credible.

items.title: PRC-linked influence operations are targeting AI debates in the US
items.bullet_md: - 🟢 **[PRC-linked influence operations are targeting AI debates in the US](https://openai.com/index/prc-linked-influence-operations-ai-debates)** — _OpenAI blog_. — OpenAI's threat intelligence team identified PRC-aligned actors generating AI-written content targeting US debates on data centers, tariffs, and tech policy. score_components.taste_reason: Concrete threat-intel report from OpenAI's team with named ops targeting US policy debates; timely and credible for AI governance readers.

items.title: How an astrophysicist uses Codex to help simulate black holes
items.bullet_md: - 🟢 **[How an astrophysicist uses Codex to help simulate black holes](https://openai.com/index/using-codex-to-simulate-black-holes)** — _OpenAI blog_. — Chi-kwan Chan uses OpenAI Codex to generate numerical relativity code for black hole accretion simulations. The AI-assisted workflow reduces iteration time from days to hours when testing predictions against Event Horizon Telescope data.

score_components.taste_reason: Nice application story (days→hours iteration) but narrow astrophysics use case; genuine signal but limited audience who will click through.

items.title: How an Agent Built a 3D Paris Gallery by Chaining Two Hugging Face Spaces
items.bullet_md: - 🟡 **[How an Agent Built a 3D Paris Gallery by Chaining Two Hugging Face Spaces](https://huggingface.co/blog/mishig/spaces-agents-md)** — _Hugging Face blog_. — Mishig Davaadorj demonstrated a coding agent autonomously building a 3D Paris monuments gallery by chaining ideogram4 for asset generation with a TRELLIS-based 3D reconstruction Space — no manual image or modeling tools touched, live at mishig/monuments-de-paris.

score_components.taste_reason: HF Spaces agent chaining demo. Novel as a demonstration but no reusable patterns or benchmarks.

items.title: Catching One in Five: LLM-as-Judge Blind Spots in Production Multi-Turn Transaction Agents
items.bullet_md: - 🧪 **[Catching One in Five: LLM-as-Judge Blind Spots in Production Multi-Turn Transaction Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10315)** — _arXiv cs.CL_. — A study of a deployed food-and-beverage ordering agent finds its built-in LLM-as-judge catches under a quarter of genuine quality defects identified by human transcript review. The finding raises questions about relying on LLM judges for production monitoring.

score_components.taste_reason: Deployed food-and-beverage ordering agent study finds LLM-as-judge catches <25% of real defects — concrete production ratio that challenges a widely-used eval pattern.
